benchmark_metadata.title: Philippine Labor Law RAG Benchmark — 100-Query Evaluation Set
benchmark_metadata.description: Benchmark dataset for evaluating the Three-Stage Hybrid RAG pipeline on Philippine labor-law question answering under multilingual and multi-turn conditions.
benchmark_metadata.labeling_notes: Each query includes gold_chunks (chunk IDs from kb/chunks/) and gold_article_refs (statute citations). reference_answer provides the canonical expected response. For multi-turn queries, conversation_history records the Phase 1 dialog (Turns 1-3); turn5_query and turn6_reference_answer extend the conversation into Phase 2 for multi-turn summarization evaluation. gold_chunks and gold_article_refs target Turn 4 (Tables 1, 2, 6); gold_chunks_turn6 and gold_article_refs_turn6 target the Turn 6 follow-up (Table 8). All 30 ambiguous queries are multi-turn: Phase 1 (Turns 1-3) is the clarification exchange enabling a ratable Turn 4 answer evaluated in Table 7; Phase 2 (Turns 5-6) tests Stage 1 history summarization evaluated in Table 8. expected_clarification is retained as a top-level reference field showing the ideal Turn 2 question.

queries.reference_answer: Ang minimum wage sa NCR ay itinatatag ng RTWPB sa pamamagitan ng Wage Orders. Ayon sa pinakabagong DOLE Handbook, ang pang-araw-araw na minimum wage ay tinukoy ayon sa sektor (non-agriculture, agriculture, atbp.) sa NCR.

queries.query_text: What does Article 99 of the Labor Code say about the minimum wage?
queries.reference_answer: Article 99 of the Labor Code (PD 442) provides that the minimum wage rates for agricultural and non-agricultural employees shall be fixed by the Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Boards.
queries.notes: Tests symbolic lookup via article_number matching. Query includes explicit 'Article 99' reference.

queries.turn5_query: If my employer has been paying me below the correct minimum wage for the past year, how long do I have to file a claim for the underpayment? Is there a deadline?
queries.turn6_reference_answer: Under Article 306 of the Labor Code (formerly Article 291 prior to renumbering), money claims arising from employer-employee relations — including underpayment of wages — must be filed within three (3) years from the time the cause of action accrued. The prescriptive period runs separately for each pay period in which underpayment occurred: the 3-year clock starts from each payroll date on which the correct minimum wage was not paid. This means if your employer has been underpaying you for the past year, you can still recover all 12 months of underpayment as long as you file within 3 years of each payroll period. Practical step: file a Request for Assistance (RFA) at the nearest DOLE Regional or Field Office under the Single Entry Approach (SEnA) — this is the mandatory first step before formal litigation before the NLRC or DOLE arbitration.

queries.query_text: Ano ang sinasabi ng Article 102 ng Labor Code tungkol sa paraan ng pagbabayad ng sahod?
queries.reference_answer: Ayon sa Article 102 ng Labor Code, ang sahod ng empleyado ay dapat bayaran sa legal tender. Hindi pinapayagan ang pagbabayad sa pamamagitan ng promissory notes, vouchers, coupons, tokens, chits, o anumang bagay maliban sa legal na pera, kahit na ito ay hiling ng empleyado.
queries.notes: Symbolic lookup: Article 102 in Filipino query triggers article_number GIN search. Replaces former Q004 (wages_minimum_wage, fil) with an explicit article citation making symbolic retrieval applicable.

queries.turn5_query: Now that I know the minimum wage rate in NCR, if my employer requires me to work on Christmas Day, which is a regular holiday, how much should I be paid for that day?
queries.turn6_reference_answer: Under Article 94 of the Labor Code and the DOLE Handbook, if you actually work on a regular holiday, you are entitled to 200% of your daily wage rate (i.e., your regular daily rate × 2). If the regular holiday also coincides with your scheduled rest day, the premium increases to 260% of your daily wage rate. This means if your daily minimum wage in NCR is the rate set under the applicable Wage Order, your pay for working on Christmas Day is twice that daily rate. If your employer does not require you to work on a regular holiday, you are still entitled to receive your regular daily rate (100%) — this is the 'no-work, still-paid' rule that applies to regular holidays for all covered employees.

queries.turn5_query: Kung ganun, paano naman kung hindi ko natanggap ang 13th month pay noong nakaraang taon? May karapatan ba ako sa kumita niyon kahit minimum wage lang ang sahod ko?
queries.turn6_reference_answer: Oo. Sa ilalim ng Presidential Decree 851, lahat ng rank-and-file employees sa private sector ay may karapatan sa 13th month pay, anuman ang antas ng sahod, kasama na ang mga minimum wage earners. Ang halaga ay katumbas ng isang-buwang basic salary (o 1/12 ng kabuuang basic pay para sa buong taon). Kung hindi ka nakatanggap ng 13th month pay noong nakaraang taon, maaari kang maghain ng reklamo sa DOLE o SEnA para mabawi ang hindi naihatid na halaga.

queries.query_text: Mahimo bang bayran ko sa akong employer og menos sa minimum wage kung apprentice ako?
queries.reference_answer: Base sa Labor Code, ang mga apprentice mahimong bayran og dili moubos sa 75% sa applicable nga minimum wage. Gikumpirma sa DOLE Handbook nga ang mga apprentice adunay katungod sa labing menos 75% sa regional minimum wage.
queries.notes: Tests hybrid: needs semantic understanding of apprentice-wage relationship plus keyword match to apprenticeship provisions. Cebuano translation — tests translation pivot.

queries.query_text: Giunsa ang pagkwenta sa Equivalent Monthly Rate (EEMR) alang sa usa ka daily-paid nga trabahante?
queries.reference_answer: Ang EEMR = (Daily Rate × Applicable Days Factor) / 12. Ang DOLE Handbook naghatag og daghang pormula depende kung ang trabahante nagtrabaho og 6 ka adlaw/semana nga adunay bayad nga holidays, o uban pang mga kahimtang.
queries.notes: Tests lexical retrieval on specific formula. Keyword 'EEMR' and 'Equivalent Monthly Rate' retained in Cebuano query; should still match handbook chunk with has_formula=true after translation pivot.

queries.query_text: Ano ang sinasabi ng Article 116 ng Labor Code tungkol sa pagpigil ng sahod ng empleyado?
queries.reference_answer: Ayon sa Article 116 ng Labor Code, ipinagbabawal ang anumang employer na pigilan o bawasan ang sahod ng empleyado maliban kung pinahihintulutan ng batas o ng empleyado mismo. Kasama dito ang pagbabawal sa wage deductions na hindi awtorisado.
queries.notes: Symbolic lookup: Article 116 in Filipino query triggers article_number GIN search. Replaces former Q010 (wages_minimum_wage, fil) with an explicit article citation. The chunk covers Articles 112-119 wage prohibitions.

queries.query_text: Pila ka oras ang normal nga adlaw sa pagtrabaho base sa balaod sa Pilipinas?
queries.reference_answer: Base sa Article 83 sa Labor Code, ang normal nga oras sa pagtrabaho dili mosobra sa 8 ka oras matag adlaw.
queries.notes: Straightforward factoid. Lexical match on 'normal work day' and 'hours'.

queries.query_text: What does Article 87 of the Labor Code provide regarding overtime work?
queries.reference_answer: Article 87 provides that work performed beyond eight hours a day shall be paid an additional compensation equivalent to the employee's regular wage plus at least twenty-five percent (25%) thereof.
queries.notes: Symbolic lookup: explicit 'Article 87' triggers article_number search.

queries.query_text: Ayon sa Article 86 ng Labor Code, magkano ang night shift differential ng isang empleyado na nagtatrabaho mula 10 PM hanggang 6 AM? Sino ang mga empleyadong hindi saklaw ng benepisyong ito?
queries.reference_answer: Ayon sa Article 86 ng Labor Code, ang night shift differential ay hindi bababa sa 10% ng regular wage ng empleyado para sa trabaho mula 10:00 PM hanggang 6:00 AM. Ang benepisyo ay hindi naaangkop sa mga empleyado ng gobyerno, kasambahay, mga managerial employees, field personnel, at mga manggagawa sa retail o service establishments na may limang empleyado o mas kaunti.
queries.notes: Retrieval target: hybrid — Explicit 'Article 86' citation enables symbolic lookup via article_number GIN search; 'night shift differential' and '10 PM hanggang 6 AM' are BM25-matchable keywords present in both the handbook and the Labor Code chunk; the coverage-exception question (who is excluded from NSD entitlement) requires semantic understanding to match the NSD exemption provisions across both chunks. Filipino query — tests translation pivot.

queries.turn5_query: If my employer refuses to pay the correct premium for that day, what are my options for recovering the underpayment?
queries.turn6_reference_answer: You should first file a Request for Assistance (RFA) under SEnA at the nearest DOLE Regional or Field Office. SEnA provides mandatory conciliation-mediation within 30 days. If conciliation fails, you may file a money claim complaint before the NLRC Regional Arbitration Branch having jurisdiction over your workplace. Money claims for unpaid wages and premium pay must be filed within three (3) years from the date each cause of action accrued (i.e., each payroll period the underpayment occurred). Retain payslips and attendance records as evidence.

queries.query_text: Ano ang mga regular holiday sa Pilipinas at magkano ang holiday pay rate?
queries.reference_answer: Sa ilalim ng Article 94 ng Labor Code, ang mga regular holiday ay kinabibilangan ng New Year's Day, Maundy Thursday, Good Friday, Araw ng Kagitingan, Labor Day, Independence Day, National Heroes Day, Bonifacio Day, Christmas Day, Rizal Day, at iba pang idineklara ng proklamasyon. Ang mga manggagawang hindi nagtrabaho ay tumatanggap ng 100% ng kanilang araw-araw na sahod; ang mga nagtrabaho ay tumatanggap ng 200%.
queries.notes: Lexical-friendly with specific keywords: 'regular holiday', 'holiday pay rate'. Filipino translation — tests translation pivot.

queries.query_text: Ilalim ng Article 93 ng Labor Code at mga patakaran ng DOLE tungkol sa premium pay, magkano ang bayad sa isang empleyado na nagtrabaho sa isang special non-working holiday? Paano kung hindi siya pumasok sa trabaho nang araw na iyon?
queries.reference_answer: Sa special non-working day, ang bayad sa manggagawang pumasok ay 130% ng kanyang daily wage. Kung hindi pumasok ang empleyado, walang bayad maliban kung may CBA o company policy na nagsasabi ng iba.
queries.notes: Retrieval target: hybrid — 'Article 93' citation triggers symbolic lookup via article_number GIN search; 'premium pay' and 'special non-working holiday' are strong BM25 keywords present in the handbook premium-pay chunk; the absence scenario ('hindi pumasok') requires semantic understanding of the no-work-no-pay rule applicable to special days, contrasting it with the worked-day rate. Filipino query — tests translation pivot.

queries.query_text: What does Article 94 of the Labor Code say about holiday pay?
queries.reference_answer: Article 94 provides that every worker shall be paid his regular daily wage during regular holidays, except in retail and service establishments regularly employing less than ten (10) workers.
queries.notes: Symbolic lookup on 'Article 94'.

queries.query_text: Usa ko ka factory worker. Ang akong employer gipugos kong magtrabaho niadtong adlaw nga opisyal nga gipahayag sa gobyerno nga walay trabaho. Pareho ra ba ang akong makuhang bayad niadtong adlawa sama sa ordinaryong adlaw sa trabaho, o adunay kalainan?
queries.reference_answer: Kung magtrabaho ka sa regular holiday, ang bayad nimo kay 200% sa imong daily rate. Kung dili ka magtrabaho, makadawat gihapon ka sa imong regular daily wage.
queries.notes: Retrieval target: dense — Cebuano query describing a government-proclaimed no-work day without using the term 'regular holiday' or citing Art. 94; paraphrases by asking whether pay differs on such days versus ordinary work days, requiring semantic understanding to match holiday pay provisions. queries.turn5_query: What if I also worked on New Year's Eve, which is a special non-working holiday, and it was not my rest day?
queries.turn6_reference_answer: For work performed on a special non-working holiday (such as New Year's Eve under Proclamation No. 9492), you are entitled to an additional 30% of your daily rate for the first 8 hours, making the total 130% of your basic daily rate. If you worked overtime on that special non-working day, the overtime premium is an additional 30% of your hourly rate for the extra hours. Note that if a special non-working day falls on your rest day, the applicable rate increases to 150% for the first 8 hours. Since New Year's Eve was not your rest day in this case, the applicable rate is 130%.

queries.notes: Retrieval target: dense — Filipino query without citing Art. 94; paraphrases 'no-work-still-paid' concept using a scenario, requiring semantic understanding to match holiday pay provisions.

Ang mga solo mother makakadawat og dugang 15 ka adlaw.

queries.reference_answer: Under RA 8972 (Solo Parents' Welfare Act), as amended by RA 11861, solo parents who have rendered at least one year of service are entitled to a parental leave of not more than seven (7) working days with pay every year.

queries.turn5_query: Am I also entitled to service incentive leave (SIL) on top of the solo parent leave?
queries.turn6_reference_answer: Yes. Under Article 95 of the Labor Code, every employee who has rendered at least one (1) year of service is entitled to five (5) days of service incentive leave (SIL) per year, which may be used as paid vacation or sick leave. This entitlement is separate from solo parent leave under RA 8972 (as amended by RA 11861). Your total paid leave entitlement therefore includes both the 7-day solo parent leave (for qualified solo parents with at least 1 year of service) and the 5-day SIL, assuming you meet the applicable tenure and qualification requirements for each.

queries.query_text: What does RA 11210 provide regarding maternity leave?
queries.reference_answer: RA 11210 (Expanded Maternity Leave Law of 2019) grants 105 days of paid maternity leave for live childbirth, 60 days for miscarriage or emergency termination, with an option to extend 30 days unpaid. Solo mothers get an additional 15 days. Allocable to the child's father: up to 7 days.

queries.query_text: What does Presidential Decree 851 provide?
queries.reference_answer: Presidential Decree No. 851 requires all employers to pay their rank-and-file employees a 13th month pay not later than December 24 of every year. The 13th month pay is defined as one-twelfth of the total basic salary earned within a calendar year.

queries.turn5_query: How many days of maternity leave am I entitled to, and will I receive full pay during that period — or only what SSS provides?
queries.turn6_reference_answer: Under RA 11210 (Expanded Maternity Leave Law), you are entitled to 105 days of paid maternity leave for a live childbirth (vaginal or caesarian). An additional 15 days is granted if you are a solo mother, and you may optionally extend your leave by 30 days without pay. Your maternity leave benefit is funded by SSS: the Daily Maternity Allowance (DMA) is computed as your average daily salary credit (ADSC) multiplied by the number of maternity leave days. Your employer is required to advance the full maternity benefit to you on or before your leave commences, then seek reimbursement from SSS. In practice, if your actual daily salary exceeds your SSS salary credit ceiling, the SSS-computed DMA may be slightly less than your full take-home pay — the law mandates at minimum the SSS-computed amount. Your employer cannot reduce your other benefits or terminate you by reason of pregnancy or maternity leave.

queries.turn6_reference_answer: The union has the following formal remedies: (1) File an Unfair Labor Practice (ULP) complaint with the NLRC. (2) If the ULP is ongoing and part of a broader pattern of union-busting, the union may file a Notice of Strike with the National Conciliation and Mediation Board (NCMB) citing ULP as a ground, as permitted under Article 278 (formerly 263) of the Labor Code. (3) The union may simultaneously file for injunctive relief or petition the NLRC to issue a cease-and-desist order against further interference. Documenting all instances of the employer's interference (including dates, names of workers called, and witness accounts) is critical for building the ULP case.

queries.turn5_query: How long do I have to file a claim for the unpaid overtime before my right to claim it prescribes?
queries.turn6_reference_answer: Under Article 306 of the Labor Code (formerly Article 291 prior to renumbering), money claims arising from employer-employee relations — including unpaid overtime pay — must be filed within three (3) years from the time the cause of action accrued. The cause of action for each unpaid overtime claim accrues on the date it should have been paid (i.e., every payroll period). This means the 3-year clock runs separately for each payroll period in which overtime was unpaid. Practical implication: if you have been underpaid on overtime for the past 2 years, you may still recover all 2 years of underpayment as long as you file within the 3-year window. Claims beyond 3 years from the payroll period are time-barred. File your RFA at SEnA now to stop the clock and preserve your right to recovery.

queries.turn5_query: In a labor-only contracting arrangement, who is responsible for remitting my SSS and PhilHealth contributions to the government agencies?

Any unremitted contributions are a serious violation and carry criminal penalties for the employer.
